answers.answer: Shuffle all four III cards and put them face down at the bottom; shuffle all nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle all three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return the unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: face-down 10-card Conflict Deck construction.

answers.answer: A human starts at 1 VP in a four-player game and 0 VP in a three-player game. Each starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third Swordmaster Agent beside the board, three troops in the nearest garrison and nine in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: Score marker is 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader; 3 troops garrison, remaining 9 in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: You may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, and after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot later take another Agent turn that round. Resolve Reveal boxes only on cards revealed for that Reveal turn, not Agent-turn cards. During Clean Up, move all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent turns optional; after a Reveal turn your turns are skipped; Reveal effects apply to just-revealed cards; Clean Up moves all cards in front to discard.

answers.answer: Resources from a Plot Intrigue played before Agent placement can join what you hold and pay that entry cost. Resources gained only after placement, from the played Agent card or destination, cannot pay that same cost. One card lets you choose only one Agent icon and send only one Agent. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn; it may only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Plot Intrigue resources before placement can pay entry; post-placement gains cannot; one Agent icon; no-icon cards only on Reveal.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, you can deploy the three troops recruited this turn plus up to two more from your garrison, for a maximum of five in this case. At a non-Combat space you cannot make normal deployment. Recruited troops are taken from your personal supply and placed in your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: current-turn recruits plus up to two from garrison at a Combat space; recruits come from supply to garrison.

answers.answer: The Spy Agent icon on the played card allows Agent access to any board space connected to an observation post where you currently have a Spy; the Spy is not recalled for this. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent, but not your own. Gather Intelligence optionally recalls a connected Spy immediately after placement, before space or card effects, to draw one card. The same Spy cannot pay both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, though two different Spies can pay the two different effects; you may get at most one Gather Intelligence draw per placement. You must decide on Gather Intelligence immediately after placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence require your Agent-turn card; Spy Agent access; at most one Gather Intelligence draw.

answers.answer: Two troops give 4 strength, one sandworm gives 3, and four revealed swords give 4, totaling 11. If your last unit is removed from the Conflict, your strength becomes 0. You cannot take part in Combat Intrigue with no unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; no units means strength 0. Combat Intrigue requires at least one unit.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you from playing again; the window closes only when all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat: players may play or pass; not required to pass after passing earlier; after Combat markers reset and units return.

answers.answer: With exactly two tied for first in a four-player Conflict, each tied player gets the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, and nobody takes the Conflict card. With the same tie in a three-player Conflict, each tied player gets the second reward, no other reward is given, and nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first with 4 players leaves others competing for third; with 3 or fewer no other rewards; no winner means no card; 0 strength receives none.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles eligible rewards; additional sandworms do not multiply them further, so two worms do not quadruple rewards. Control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 1 VP for 3 spice, you may pay the cost a second time to gain it again: 3 spice for 1 VP, or 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more doubles; control and battle icons cannot; may pay optional reward cost a second time.

answers.answer: After winning a Conflict, take its card face up into your supply, then check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply with a matching icon. A matching pair must be flipped face down and scores 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild battle icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply; flip the pair face down for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: take won card, then mandatory matching-pair check; Endgame wild icon may match any of three.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if Influence falls below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first to 4 also gets the Alliance token and its 1 VP; that VP follows the token. Tying the current holder does not take it: you must rise above the holder. The FAQ separately says that if the holder loses Influence after having been tied, a formerly tied opponent takes it; the old holder loses the VP and the new holder gains it. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, the token returns to the board and its VP is lost.
answers.evidence: Scoring: Faction Influence and Alliance token; tie does not steal; FAQ holder-loses-Influence transfer rule.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, you may spend Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card or split one source among different cards. The Imperium Row refills to five after an acquisition, so you may buy its replacement immediately if you can afford it. Put an acquired card face up in your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Persuasion timing, pooling/splitting, Row replacement, acquired card to discard.

answers.answer: At an unoccupied Maker space, add one bonus spice during Makers; when visiting, collect all bonus spice there. Deep Desert costs 3 water and gives 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and gives 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Hooks are required only where the summoning effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. The Shield Wall prevents summoning to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin until removed. A summoned worm goes directly into your quadrant of the Conflict and can never be put in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers; Sandworms: placement, Hooks requirements, Shield Wall; Board Space Guide Deep Desert and Hagga Basin.

answers.answer: At the end of a round, 10 or more VP for any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards, then highest VP wins. The rulebook tiebreakers, in order, are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: game end at end of round; Endgame Intrigue before winner; tiebreakers.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM uses 20 standard contracts: shuffle them and expose two face up, leaving 18 face down in the bank. Add the four CHOAM Intrigue cards to the Intrigue Deck and four CHOAM Imperium cards to the Imperium Deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are a separate Rise of Ix compatibility set and stay out of standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module setup changes; contrasting-back contracts are a separate Rise of Ix set.

answers.answer: With CHOAM and a public face-up contract available, take one into your supply and refill that offer face up from the bank if possible. If no public offer remains, gain 2 Solari; Shaddam's reserved contracts do not prevent this fallback for other players. A Harvest contract is completed by visiting a Maker space and gaining the printed amount of spice that turn in total, including other sources. Immediate is completed as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow is completed when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts; Completing contracts; shared Human contract icon rule.

answers.answer: No. A space contract taken after you already sent your Agent to that space cannot be completed until a future turn, because you must have held it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: must hold it when sending Agent; announce, gain rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It receives the Ornithopter Objective. First Player goes to the human whose Objective shows the marker; First Player alternates only between the two humans. Turn order is First Player, Rival, other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: standard two-player setup, Objective, First Player and turn order; Rival never takes Reveal turn.

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type; if none exists, ignore placement. Either way reveal another card and continue the Agent turn. Ignore normal space costs and effects; apply only revealed House Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination; Place Spy cards; ignore normal space costs/effects; reshuffle when empty or Reshuffle appears.

answers.answer: For three or four players, remove Objectives whose 1-3P/4/6P marking does not fit, shuffle the eligible cards, and deal one face up to each player. The player whose Objective shows the First Player marker takes it. Shaddam may not be used without the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched Objective cards, distribute one random face up and award First Player; do not use Shaddam unless CHOAM.

answers.answer: The bank's Solari, spice, water, and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if the bank runs out. Troops are limited by the player's supply: if it is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Resource payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: bank resources and sandworms not meant to be limited; troop recruitment; gains from and payments to bank.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict card face up next to the deck, resolve any controlled-location defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, humans return Agents to Leaders; with 3–4 humans pass First Player clockwise, while in two-player play return Rival Agents to its supply and pass First Player to the other human, never the Rival; then start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: phases and Round Start; Recall: next-round preparation.

answers.answer: Yes. After paying entry costs and meeting requirements before placement, board-space effects and the played card's Agent-box effects may be carried out in any order, and the Faction advance is part of those visit effects. You cannot use Influence gained from that visit to meet its own entry requirement because requirements must be met before effects resolve.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements before effects; space, card and Influence effects may be in any order.

answers.answer: No. An arrow cost and its effect may be used only once per turn, even if you have enough to pay twice; the exception is sandworm reward doubling on a Conflict reward. Most card and space effects are mandatory, with exceptions such as “may,” optional arrow costs, and the optional black-X trash icon. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ: Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: A Spy placement icon lets you put a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If a placement effect specifies an Agent icon that must connect to the post, that connection is required or placement is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts; placement effect may require a particular connected Agent icon.

answers.answer: You cannot Infiltrate your own occupied space; Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent. A Spy does not let you place an Agent without playing a card and meeting its normal Agent access condition. You cannot recall two Spies for two Gather Intelligence draws on one placement; only one such draw is allowed.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Infiltrate; Gather Intelligence; separate Spy costs and Spy Agent access.

answers.answer: When anyone visits a controlled Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, its controller separately gains 1 Solari; at Imperial Basin the controller gains 1 spice. The visitor also gets the space's visit effects, even if the controller is the visitor. A winning critical-location Conflict puts your Control marker there, replacing the opponent's marker. When a Conflict is revealed for a location you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict, without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: controlled-location visitor bonuses; Critical Locations & Control: control and defensive troop.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player receives the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps the first reward and card, and no further rewards are given. Players tied for third receive nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward; nobody wins or takes the card and no other rewards are given, including in a four-player game with one remaining player.
answers.evidence: Combat ties and Three tied for first table.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive rewards; third gets nothing. The same ordinary rank rewards apply in a two-player game with a Rival: first and second receive rewards, third receives none except that third reward is used for a tie for second.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: in 2 or 3 players ordinary first and second receive rewards; third only in tie for second.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat only if you have at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep Intrigues face down and separate from your deck, and reveal only when playing; after resolving, place them face up in an Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue Deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards; FAQ Draw timing: if Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle discard to form new deck.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand, not an Intrigue unless specified; it does not discard a card in play or in your discard pile. A separate trash-an-Intrigue icon lets you trash one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets' steal icon takes one Intrigue at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigue cards.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Trashing; Intrigue cards: Steal Intrigue icon.

answers.answer: Trash effects can remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or instructed to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow's acquire VP remains even if that card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ Victory: The Spice Must Flow's acquire VP is retained if later trashed.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once, at the moment you acquire that card, not when you later play it. If you need to draw while your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved; it is lost after your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards: reshuffle when deck empty and unused Persuasion is lost.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on your Reveal turn remain face up and in play through the Reveal turn, so Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play. Two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another regardless of order played. They cease being in play when all cards in front of you move to your discard pile at Clean Up, unless trashed first.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: cards from Agent and Reveal turns stay in play through Clean Up; two Bond cards activate each other.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed this turn; that Agent may be used on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop moves from the Conflict back to your garrison. “Retreat any number” can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A free-choice effect granting two Influence assigns both to one chosen Faction; it cannot split them across two Factions. An Alliance icon requires you to hold that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires the stated minimum with its specified Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence: free-choice gain two cannot choose different Factions; Alliance icon and minimum Influence requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after two opponents were tied with them, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if several opponents were tied, the former holder chooses the recipient. The former holder loses 1 VP and the recipient gains 1 VP. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more Influence, the token returns to the board and the holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring: official FAQ separate transfer trigger and return-to-board rule.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards drawn at Round Start. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until that effect applies, is used then, and is discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. An Intrigue requiring that you win cannot be played after tying for first, because nobody won. If you receive that Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, it can be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: “When you win a Conflict” Intrigues cannot be played after a first-place tie; may play if received as winning reward.

answers.answer: If final VP and all four listed tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track's 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts you hold for that space with the same Agent placement; you cannot delay them. A board-space contract is another effect of the Agent turn and can resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, but you must have held it when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not start with the two set-aside Sardaukar contracts; they are reserved for his exclusive acquisition. When he acquires a contract, he may choose one of them instead of a public contract. His Emperor of the Known Universe restriction applies immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts only for that turn, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup; Reserved Sardaukar contracts; FAQ Shaddam.

answers.answer: During setup, put Feyd's token on the leftmost Training track space; on reaching the rightmost it stays there for the rest of the game. Lady Jessica begins with the Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ Reverend Mother Jessica.

answers.answer: Yes, moving from 1 to 3 while gaining multiple Influence counts as reaching 2. You may reach 2 with the same Faction again after losing Influence and later moving back up; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from your hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract is a Spice Trade space, with no cost and no Combat deployment: always draw one card, and resolve the contract icon. Dutiful Service is an Emperor space, with no cost and no Combat deployment: gain one Emperor Influence and resolve the contract icon. Without CHOAM, the icon gives 2 Solari. With CHOAM, take and refill a public contract if available; otherwise gain 2 Solari. Only Dutiful Service automatically advances a Faction track, by one Emperor Influence; Accept Contract gives none.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Faction status and shared contract icon rule; space table.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City access, no cost, Combat space; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while its controller gets 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat space; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw one card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat space; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; choose 4 base spice or, if you have Hooks, summon two worms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon one worm. At either space you collect all bonus spice there regardless of choosing worms. Hooks are retained, not spent. The Shield Wall prevents summoning to protected Conflicts at the three named locations while it remains.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Sandworms: Hooks retained and Shield Wall restriction.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and at least 2 Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. The first takes Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruits one troop, and gains 1 water. The second gains 1 water and optionally removes the Shield Wall; it does not recruit a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr.

answers.answer: High Council is Landsraad access, costs 5 Solari each visit, and is not a Combat space. On the first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On subsequent visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains a Swordmaster and 6 after anyone has one. Each player may visit it only once per game. Take the third Agent from beside the board onto your Leader; it is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival gaining Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege is Landsraad access, costs 3 Solari, requires 2 or more Emperor Influence, and is not a Combat space. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege; Faction status notes.

answers.answer: Shipping is Spice Trade access, costs 3 spice, requires 2 or more Spacing Guild Influence, and is not a Combat space. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; that free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad, non-Combat, and lets you choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari: recruit two troops either way; paying 2 also gains 1 water. Spice Refinery is City, a Combat space, and lets you choose to pay 0 or 1 spice: gain 2 Solari free or 4 Solari if paying 1; its controller also gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner is Spacing Guild access, costs 5 spice, gives 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops; it is a Combat space. Desert Tactics is Fremen access, costs 1 water, gives 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and optionally trashes a card; it is a Combat space. Sardaukar is Emperor access, costs 4 spice, gives 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops; it is not a Combat space.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad access, no cost, non-Combat: draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage is Bene Gesserit access, costs 1 spice, non-Combat: gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild access, no cost, non-Combat: gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. Assembly Hall's Persuasion applies during the Reveal turn when its Agent is there.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. During Reveal, ignore Litany Against Fear's red box; alternatively, if it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card, ignore that red box then.
answers.evidence: FAQ: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Manipulate prevents opponents from acquiring the removed card. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it is not acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Manipulate.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four Influence cubes, one at the bottom of each Faction track; three troops in its garrison and nine in supply; two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board; three Spies and 1 water in supply; score and Combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and keep the 2P Reshuffle card in its deck. The Rival can trigger Endgame at 10 or more VP and can win by having the most VP.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: setup and starting components; Rival 10+ VP triggers Endgame.

answers.answer: As soon as its total Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water reaches its printed Swordmaster value, it spends exactly that amount and gains its third Agent for use in the current round. Count each unit/card as one, including starting water. Mandatory payment order is Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, then water; use as much of each as needed before moving to the next, stop when paid, and keep leftovers. It cannot choose a different mix to preserve higher-priority resources.
answers.evidence: Swordmaster resource total and mandatory spending priority.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends each set of 7 Solari, each set of 7 spice, each set of 3 Intrigue cards, or each set of 3 water for 1 VP. It cannot combine unlike resources into a mixed total of seven for one VP.
answers.evidence: After Swordmaster: whenever Rival has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence and breaks ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains Influence VP and Alliances like a human, including 1 VP at 2 and Alliance VP, but receives no resource bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in the Rival card's Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: Influence choice; After Swordmaster; Rival Agent turns: numbered Influence icon.

answers.answer: No. With a two-destination card, select only the destination matching current conditions—Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, or Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner. If the selected destination is occupied, reveal another Hagal card without using the other destination.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination card selection and occupied destination.

answers.answer: At every Rival Combat space, it may deploy up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited by a card at a non-Combat space go into its garrison. A conditional bonus at 2+ Influence does not prevent placement; if the Rival lacks the Influence, it simply does not get that bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: recruit/deploy rules; unmet 2+ Influence bonus does not prevent Agent placement.

answers.answer: When no post type is specified, the Rival places a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Rival's Agent reaches a Combat space that turn, those troops can deploy there too. If a Place Spy card finds no legal post, ignore placement, reveal another Hagal card, and continue the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Place Spy card behavior.

answers.answer: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, the Rival collects all bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one worm at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of taking base spice. If it summons none—because it lacks Hooks or the Conflict is protected—it takes the base spice instead: 2 at Hagga, 4 at Deep Desert. Hooks are its own and are retained. Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: Hooks, worms, base spice and accumulated bonus spice.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords as strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window and can respond afterward. A Rival with no deployed unit does not get this bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: strength bonus and Reshuffle; humans then have normal window.

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival can gain control bonuses, defensive troops, battle-icon VP, and normal sandworm reward doubling. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay the resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts: a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: control, defensive troop, battle icons, doubling, optional Conflict VP and contracts.

answers.answer: During Reveal Effects, total and announce Combat strength and set the marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed during the Reveal turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip to the +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: total, announce and set strength at any point; Strength: over 20 track procedure.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not when merely revealing the card. Card text can override the game's usual rules.
answers.evidence: Setup: Signet Ring icon activates on Agent turn, not reveal; Overview: cards can override usual rules.

answers.answer: The Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. It does not by itself mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate effects requiring their stated connected-post conditions and decisions.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Recall Spy icon; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence rules.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard-a-card instruction instead discards a card of your choice from your hand, and cannot discard an Intrigue unless specified.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: A sandworm doubles the Conflict reward, and a reward granting one Influence of your choice therefore grants two Influence; those may go to the same Faction or to two different Factions. This differs from one effect that directly grants two free-choice Influence, which must put both into one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example; Influence free-choice rule.

answers.answer: Resolve the Signet Ring ability printed on the selected Rival card. Do not substitute its Scheme. The Rival needs neither a human Signet Ring card nor a Reveal turn; the Hagal Signet Ring icon triggers that ability.
answers.evidence: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme are separate abilities.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon gives the Rival a token if it lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no second token. Shield Wall removal works only if it has Hooks and the Wall remains. Without Hooks it is ignored; if the Wall is already gone there is no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets is Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost, and is not a Combat space. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; in addition, each opponent with four or more Intrigues gives one chosen at random to you.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Secrets; Steal Intrigue icon rule.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin is Spice Trade access, costs nothing, and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there. Its controller gains 1 spice, even when the visitor and controller are the same player, so that player receives both visit and control gains.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Basin and controlled-location rule.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict from the top and place it face up next to the Conflict Deck, on top of any Conflict cards remaining from earlier rounds. Each player then draws five cards from their own deck to form their hand; this occurs after the Conflict reveal and defensive bonus.
answers.evidence: Round Start: reveal new Conflict on top of prior unresolved cards; then each player draws five.

answers.answer: Each human begins with one Influence cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction tracks. The four Alliance tokens begin on their marked track spaces; no human starts holding one. The Shield Wall token is initially placed in the marked area below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup: Shield Wall and Alliance token placement; four cubes on bottom spaces.

answers.answer: First Player takes the first turn, then play proceeds clockwise, one Agent or Reveal turn at a time. Once a player Reveals, their turns are skipped; in standard 3–4-player play Player Turns end when all have Revealed. During Combat Intrigue, First Player acts first and priority proceeds clockwise. An eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues, or pass; passing earlier does not prevent acting again, and the window ends after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat Intrigue window.

answers.answer: The steps are Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, then Clean Up. Reveal all remaining hand cards face up; resolve only those cards' Reveal boxes and use Persuasion to acquire cards, in any order; then move all cards in front of you to your discard pile. Reveal effects need not be resolved in card order; you may choose their order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: three steps and effects may resolve in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's 10-card starting deck and place it face down in their supply left of the Leader. Without CHOAM, omit marked cards, shuffle the Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down, deal five face-up Imperium Row cards, and place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. The human Combat marker starts at 0 with the initial side shown in the rulebook face up; three Spies and the Councilor start in personal supply in clear view; three Control markers also start in personal supply.
answers.evidence: Setup and Initial card states; Human component layout.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, Persuasion may acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards, Prepare the Way, or The Spice Must Flow. The cost is shown at the card's top right. Ordinary Persuasion purchases are made during the Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional, so you may decline even if a legal placement or recall exists. A Shield Wall detonation icon lets you remove the token; the summary says you may remove it, so it is optional. Once removed, it is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy placement/recall optional; Shield Wall removal is permanent; FAQ optional effects.

answers.answer: The played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination's upper-left access icon, or a Spy Agent icon permitting access through a Spy at a connected post. A Spy connected to Shipping does not make a City-only card legal for Shipping. If the card has the Spy Agent icon and you have a Spy at a post connected to Shipping, you may use that Spy access without recalling the Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: matching icon requirement; separate Spy costs and Spy Agent access.

answers.answer: Yes. You may first play a legal Plot Intrigue during your Agent turn before placing your Agent; resources it grants before placement can pay the entry cost. Resources from the card played to send the Agent or from the destination are gained only after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Plot Intrigue before placement can fund entry; post-placement effects cannot.

answers.answer: No. After both humans have Revealed, Player Turns continue while the Rival still has an Agent in supply. The Rival keeps taking Agent turns until it has used all Agents; only then does play proceed to Combat. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: in two-player play, continue Rival Agent turns after humans Reveal; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: Standard 2–4-player board spaces and access/combat status: Accept Contract—Spice Trade, no; Arrakeen—City, yes; Assembly Hall—Landsraad, no; Deep Desert—Spice Trade, yes; Deliver Supplies—Spacing Guild, no; Desert Tactics—Fremen, yes; Dutiful Service—Emperor, no; Espionage—Bene Gesserit, no; Fremkit—Fremen, yes; Gather Support—Landsraad, no; Hagga Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Heighliner—Spacing Guild, yes; High Council—Landsraad, no; Imperial Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Imperial Privilege—Landsraad, no; Research Station—City, yes; Sardaukar—Emperor, no; Secrets—Bene Gesserit, no; Shipping—Spice Trade, no; Sietch Tabr—City, yes; Spice Refinery—City, yes; Swordmaster—Landsraad, no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Agent access icon and Combat? columns for 22 spaces.

answers.answer: At Round Start, when a Conflict for a location already controlled is revealed, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict without an Agent visit. After Conflict rewards, return troops from the Conflict to supply, return sandworms to the bank, and reset all Combat markers to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive troop bonus; Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: For an ordinary Agent turn, play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching board space. Resolve the played card's Agent box and ignore its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in your discard pile for this turn; you must play from hand. The Agent must come from your Leader, so you cannot simply move an Agent already on the board (unless an effect recalls an other Agent as a distinct action).
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one card from hand, Agent from Leader, use Agent box; Recall Agent exception.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent, for the entire turn. Resolving board-space effects first cannot postpone it, so he cannot deploy units before the restriction starts.
answers.evidence: Shaddam Leader clarification: restriction takes effect immediately; cannot postpone by ordering effects.

answers.answer: With four players at four different positive strengths and no sandworms, first, second, and third place receive their corresponding printed rewards; fourth receives none. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up, then checks for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: 4-player first/second/third rewards; winner takes card; fourth unlisted receives no reward.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup: each player takes a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, not the Imperium Deck. If your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and draw; you cannot choose a card directly from your discard pile instead.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards: ordinary draw uses your own deck; reshuffle discard when empty.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. It is not removed.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup: shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A player who later acquires one moves it from the bank onto their garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup: all Maker Hooks in common bank; acquired token moves to player's garrison.

answers.answer: The marker must be adjusted when the Combat Intrigue resolves during the Combat Intrigue window; Reveal-turn strength is not fixed for the round. Resolve rewards using the adjusted strength shown on the Combat track after all eligible players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: adjust marker when card resolves; then resolve using adjusted strength.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice, and water come from the bank. The rules do not instruct taking resources from another player's supply; payments return resources to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: whenever you gain resources take from bank; payments return to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contract tokens face down before exposing two face up on the marked board spaces; place the rest face down in the bank. Players do not choose the offers or preset their order. If Shaddam is chosen, set aside both Sardaukar contracts first, then shuffle the other 18 and expose two; 16 remain face down in bank.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes: shuffle contract tokens face down, then flip two offers; Shaddam exception.

answers.answer: If Shaddam is chosen, set aside both standard Sardaukar contracts before the contract shuffle. Only Shaddam may acquire them, and they do not begin in his possession. Shuffle the remaining 18 contracts, expose two face up, and put the other 16 face down in the bank, with the two reserved contracts set aside.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes; Reserved Sardaukar contracts.
